easy_fields.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
easy_fields.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
easy_fields.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines and 30 subjects.

G3_collection.reasoning: The paper extensively details the data collection methodology, including sources (college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources), the number of annotators (50 college students), and the multi-stage collection process.

G4_annotation.reasoning: The paper describes a detailed annotation protocol, including guidelines for annotators, quality control steps, and considerations for data contamination during the annotation process.

G5_rai.reasoning: The paper discusses limitations of the benchmark, potential biases from manual curation, ethical considerations regarding copyright and data privacy, and data contamination concerns, along with an error analysis that highlights model shortcomings.

G6_processing.reasoning: The paper describes data cleaning and categorization as preprocessing steps, outlines evaluation pipelines for different question types, and mentions a version change log, indicating maintenance and release planning.
